task: Remove Brazil-only location blockers from producer activation while preserving Brazil CEP/city assistance as an optional compatibility path
implemented: Preserve alphanumeric/international postal codes instead of coercing every value into an 8-digit CEP
Expose Brazilian CEP lookup only when the entered value actually matches CEP format
Allow manual city and region values without requiring an IBGE city id before production creation
Keep Brazilian city catalog lookup as optional enrichment
Allow international region names instead of a two-character UF-only field
Remove pt-BR hardcode from city normalization in production creation
Record catalog/manual/not-provided location resolution in existing activation telemetry

deployment.note: Both deployment attempts built and copied the exact merged SHA successfully, but the automated public health check failed both times. No manual VPS access was used.

measurement.note: No conversion lift is claimed before real post-release data exists.

remaining_global_gap: The frontend no longer blocks foreign/manual locations, but the current API still exposes Brazil-specific location lookup endpoints and lacks a verified first-class country/timezone/locale/currency location contract. Full end-to-end internationalization remains a backend/platform follow-up.
handoff: Infrastructure/operations owner: investigate the persistent production HTTP health-check failure for SHA 312dd026ccbe5928199bf3449d49fa72a1149f4d using deploy run 36095425114. Validate and Lighthouse are green and application copy succeeded twice, so do not assume a frontend regression without evidence.

Backend/global architecture owner: introduce a first-class configurable country/timezone/locale/currency location contract before claiming complete global location support; preserve backward compatibility with existing Brazilian CEP/IBGE assistance.
expected_impact: Reduce production-creation abandonment for producers outside Brazil and keep the activation path compatible with international locations.
